company_items.summary: AutoZone posted a fiscal Q4 EPS beat of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but quality was poor — the upside was driven by tariff refunds adding 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO benefit adding another 105 basis points. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% versus the expected +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex deeper into the robotics and AI-driven automation space.

MillerKnoll reported a solid fiscal Q1 EPS beat of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even without tariff refunds — stripping out the 11-cent tailwind, adjusted EPS was still 42 cents versus 36 cents expected. Sales disappointed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the $943.2 million consensus, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was left unchanged at $1.85–$2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings extensive experience, having previously served as CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The move provides leadership clarity for the company.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS expectations, reporting 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% well below the 13.85% consensus estimate. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure weighing on household budgets and retail demand, and will not provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost-reduction actions underway, and a North American towable RV order backlog surging approximately 75% year-over-year.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The strong efficacy data reinforces Viking's position as a credible competitor in the increasingly crowded but highly valuable obesity and metabolic disease treatment market. This is a significant clinical milestone for the company.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is an earnings-focused note covering Tuesday September 22nd before the open. There is no broad macro or Fed commentary in this morning's release, so let's go straight to the company-specific action — and there's plenty of it across six names.

Starting with AutoZone, the stock posted a fiscal fourth quarter earnings beat — $56.05 versus the $54.03 consensus — but do not get excited about the quality here. The upside was entirely manufactured by tariff refunds, which added 145 basis points to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture is much weaker. Domestic comps came in at just plus 1.6% against expectations of plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales trends in the back half of the quarter and said they feel well positioned heading into fiscal 2027, but this is a low-quality beat and traders should treat it as such.

Cognex is making a bold move into robotics and Physical AI, announcing the acquisition of RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception — for roughly $500 million upfront plus an additional $106 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic offensive play into a high-growth area.

MillerKnoll delivered a genuine earnings beat — 53 cents versus 36 cents expected — and importantly, the beat holds up even after stripping out tariff refund benefits. Adjusted, they earned 42 cents against a 36-cent bar. The problem is the top line, which missed and fell 3.3% organically. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed slightly, though earnings per share guidance was left unchanged. Mixed picture overall.

Pentair has resolved its CFO uncertainty, naming Bob Hau — a veteran who previously held the CFO role at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox — effective November 1st. Clean leadership transition, modestly positive.

THOR Industries missed on fiscal fourth quarter earnings — 78 cents versus 87 expected — as gross margins collapsed 230 basis points below consensus. Management's tone was cautious, flagging macro headwinds across rates, fuel, and consumer budgets. They will not provide fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. On the positive side, dealer inventories are healthy, cost restructuring is underway, and North American towable RV order backlog surged 75% year-over-year. A complicated print — not a clean short, but not a buy either.

Finally, the standout mover of the morning: Viking Therapeutics is spiking hard in pre-market after reporting 22% weight loss results from its GLP-1 drug VK2735 trial. This is a significant efficacy readout and puts Viking firmly on the map as a serious player in the obesity drug race. Watch for sector-wide read-throughs in GLP-1 names today.

Bottom line: the session opens with a volatile mix — a low-quality beat from AutoZone, a strategic acquisition from Cognex, a genuine beat from MillerKnoll offset by soft sales, a miss from THOR, and a major catalyst from Viking. No macro commentary today, so price action will be stock-specific. Stay disciplined and size accordingly.
